question: A shared .mcp.json points a stdio server's args at ${API_REGION:-us-east-1}. On a machine where the API_REGION environment variable is unset, what value does Claude Code pass to the server?
options: A) The literal string us-east-1, because the ${VAR:-default} syntax falls back to the default when the variable is not set
B) An empty string, because Claude Code always expands an unset variable to blank rather than substituting the trailing default text
C) The literal text ${API_REGION:-us-east-1}, because default-value expansion only applies inside the env block and not in args
D) A parse failure, because Claude Code requires every referenced environment variable to be set even when a default is supplied
correct_answers: A) The literal string us-east-1, because the ${VAR:-default} syntax falls back to the default when the variable is not set
explanations: Correct. ${VAR:-default} expands to the variable's value when it is set and to the text after :- when it is not, so with API_REGION unset the server receives the literal us-east-1. Claude Code's MCP documentation lists args among the fields where this expansion happens, alongside command, env, url, and headers.

Claude Code does not blank out a referenced variable that carries a default; the whole purpose of the :- form is to substitute the text after :- instead of an empty value. Nothing in the documented expansion rules yields an empty string here.
Expansion is not confined to the env block. The documented expansion locations are command, args, env, url, and headers, so a value inside args is substituted like any other.

No failure occurs: a default was supplied, which is exactly what :- is for. Even with no default at all the file still parses — Claude Code loads the config, reports a missing-variable warning for that server in claude mcp list, and passes the unexpanded ${VAR} text through.
